questions.question: What is the capital of the Republic of Ireland?
questions.explanation: Dublin is the capital of the Republic of Ireland. Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, which is part of the UK.

questions.question: What is the difference between the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland?
options: The Republic is an independent state; Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom
They are two names for the same country
Northern Ireland is independent; the Republic belongs to the UK
Both are part of the United Kingdom
questions.explanation: The Republic of Ireland (Éire) is an independent state covering about 5/6 of the island, while Northern Ireland is part of the UK.

questions.question: What was The Great Famine (1845-1852)?
options: A catastrophic famine in Ireland that killed many and forced mass emigration
A war between Ireland and Scotland
A period of great economic growth
questions.explanation: The Great Famine was a disaster where the potato crops failed. Around a million people died and many more emigrated, especially to America.

questions.question: What ended the conflict known as "The Troubles" in Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: The Good Friday Agreement (1998) brought peace after about 30 years of conflict (1968-1998) between groups in Northern Ireland.

questions.question: Which of these are national symbols of Ireland?
options: The maple leaf and the eagle
questions.explanation: The shamrock (three-leaf clover) and the harp are Ireland's national symbols. St Patrick's Day on 17 March is the national day.
